security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel does not save/restore all CHERI capability register state (capability data, bounds, permissions, tags, CIFC level metadata from uycfg) during context switch between userspace processes, or under Zyhybrid, fails to scrub capability registers when switching from a CHERI (RVY64I) process to a non-CHERI (RV64I) process, exposing capability state across the security boundary
security_spec.summary: Kernel must atomically save/restore all CHERI capability register file on context switch and scrub on Zyhybrid RVY-to-RV64I transitions, or capability metadata leaks between processes

findings.finding: thread_struct has no CHERI capability register fields (no capdata, bounds, permissions, tags, or uycfg metadata). Any CHERI/RVY capability state in hardware registers has no kernel-side backing store to save/restore across context switches.

__switch_to saves/restores only callee-saved GPRs (ra, sp, s0-s11) and SUM status bit. No CHERI capability registers (CLEN-bit-wide cap regs, UYCFG, or any RVY-specific CSRs) are saved or restored. On CHERI hardware, capability tags/bounds/metadata would leak across process boundaries.
findings.snippet:
SYM_FUNC_START(__switch_to)
	REG_S ra,  TASK_THREAD_RA_RA(a3)
	REG_S sp,  TASK_THREAD_SP_RA(a3)
	REG_S s0,  TASK_THREAD_S0_RA(a3)
	/* ... only callee-saved GPRs, no CHERI cap regs ... */
	REG_L s11, TASK_THREAD_S11_RA(a4)
	ret
SYM_FUNC_END(__switch_to)

findings.finding: switch_to() macro calls __switch_to_fpu, __switch_to_vector, and __switch_to_envcfg, but has no capability-state save/restore callout. The Zyhybrid 'scrub on CHERI->non-CHERI transition' requirement has no corresponding implementation. If a CHERI (RVY64I) process context-switches to a non-CHERI (RV64I) process on Zyhybrid hardware, capability register state persists uncleaned.

hwcap.h defines 110+ ISA extensions (Z*, S*, X*), but no RVY* or CHERI capability-related ISA extension constants exist. No RVY64I, RVYA25 profile, Zyhybrid, or any CHERI encoding identifier is defined. Detection of CHERI-capable harts is impossible, so capability-aware save/restore paths cannot be gated.

KVM VCPU context switch saves/restores standard GPRs and basic CSRs (sstatus, stvec, sscratch, sepc) but has no CHERI capability register save/restore. A VM using CHERI userspace would leak capability state across VM exits/resumes.
findings.snippet:
.macro SAVE_HOST_GPRS
	REG_S ra, (KVM_ARCH_HOST_RA)(a0)
	/* ... only standard GPRs, no CHERI cap regs ... */
.endm
.macro RESTORE_GUEST_GPRS
	REG_L ra, (KVM_ARCH_GUEST_RA)(a0)
	/* ... only standard GPRs, no CHERI cap regs ... */
.endm

findings.finding: start_thread() initializes FPU and CFI state for new userspace processes but does not initialize or clear CHERI capability registers (PCC, capability GPR metadata/tags). A CHERI process exec'd into a non-CHERI process on Zyhybrid hardware would inherit stale capability state from the exec context.

Signal delivery saves/restores FPU and vector state to the signal frame, but has no CHERI capability register save/restore. A signal delivered to a CHERI process that runs a signal handler would see capability register corruption, and the sigreturn path would not restore capability metadata.
